newsitem.title: USA: AmEx, Credomatic launch dual currency card product.
newsitem.headline: AmEx, Credomatic launch dual currency card product.

text.p: American Express Co cards to be offered in five Central American countries with partner Credomatic will allow customers to pay bills in local currencies or U.S. dollars, executives of the companies said Thursday.

"What this does now is enable us ... (to issue cards) billed in local currencies for local spending and in dollars outside of the country," Jonathan Linen, vice chairman of American Express said in a telephone conference call with reporters. He said customers can repay in either currency.

Ernesto Castegnaro, chief executive of Credomatic, said while many people in the region already have U.S. dollar-denominated American Express cards, they prefer not to use them for local transactions. He predicted the new product will be well received by customers but did not make specific projections.
Existing American Express customers in the five countries will have the option of converting their card to the new product, retaining the existing card, or carrying both.
Linen declined to discuss financial details of the arrangement with Credomatic, which was first announced in January. But he said it was attractive for both parties.

Credomatic is a privately-held company headquartered in San Jose, Costa Rica. It describes itself as the leading card issuer in Central America with a network of more than 36,000 merchants and more than 700,000 cards in its portfolio. It also issues Visa and MasterCards.

Customers in Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador will be offered American Express green and gold cards and a revolving credit card. The products will be offered later in the year in El Salvador but the launch in the other four countries was formally kicked off Thursday. The credit line will be offered by Credomatic.
James Cracchiolo, president of American Express global network services group, said two additional announcements of partnershps will be announced in coming weeks.
Linen said there are more than 20 institutions issuing cards on the American Express network currently, and added, "as we speak we are in conversations with probably double that number right now."
